newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London firm after second land auction.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London firm after second land auction.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks firmed in London on Tuesday, buoyed by shares in property developers, following a successful land auction conducted after the market closed in Hong Kong, dealers said.

Earlier in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index fell 230.73 points, or 1.54 per cent, to close at 14,760.17, after an initially disappointing response to the last land auction to be held before Chinese rule.

But enthusiastic bidding for a waterfront site at Hunghom in the auction staged during London trading hours, boosted shares in property developers which dragged the Hang Seng London Reference Index 25.93 points higher to close at 14,786.10.

Shares in Cheung Kong and Hutchison Whampoa both advanced as they teamed together to snap up the waterfront site for HK6.06 billion. Cheung Kong climbed HK$1.05 to HK$78.8 and Hutchison rose 75 cents to HK$65.00.

Elsewhere, weakness of shares in HSBC Holdings in Hong Kong spilled over into the London session. The heavyweight banking group slid HK$3.50 to HK$223.5 as profit takers took advantage of recent strong gains in the shares.
-- Andrew Langlands, London Newsroom +44 171 542 3496 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
